item.title: The legacy of Mr. Paul Tepatul: How a son immortalized “Tisa Paul”
item.description: How often do you read stories of Papua New Guinean children writing the life histories of their parents? If you have come across one, you are fortunate; but if you haven’t, look no further than the book titled “TISA PAUL.” This book is dedicated to a father who devoted 40 years of his life to teaching the nation’s future generations in the rugged interior of the Western Highlands Province. item.title: Solar power transforms teaching and learning in Huon Gulf
item.description: The Light for Learning project, through the Papua New Guinea-Australia Partnership, has installed solar systems for 8,095 homes and nearly 273 community facilities across the Huon Gulf District, Morobe Province. item.title: Local Community defends Badili
item.description: Tensions remain high in Moresby South today as the Gorobe Talai community at Badili successfully mobilised to prevent the evicted 2-Mile Hill settlers from encroaching on their section. While chaos spread across the district, the Gorobe Talai residents took a firm stand to secure their boundaries, ensuring that those displaced by the evictions did not settle in their section. item.title: GFI Launches ‘Skel Skul’ competition 2026 to support schools and students
item.description: Goodman Fielder International (GFI) today launched its Skel Skul Competition 2026, an initiative designed to support parents and schools by encouraging the purchase of Skel Rice. The program, according to GFI, is a nationwide initiative designed to empower the future leaders of Papua New Guinea. item.title: Child displaced with mother missing out on school
item.description: THERE is little hope remaining for a grieving mother to allow her son to continue Grade Seven after losing everything. item.title: Women’s division hit finals in Wau tournament
item.description: Women’s football has taken centre stage at the Kumul Blo Space Soccer Tournament in Wau as the competition reaches the semi-final stage, highlighting the growing strength and confidence of female players in the district. Four teams have qualified for the Women’s Semi-Finals. WH Neighbour’s will take on Elek Sisters in the first semi-final match, and WWD Admin will face Hawe United from Kaindi in the second semi-final.
